articles.title: Why your LLM is slow twice, and why it runs out of memory: prefill, decode and the KV cache
articles.excerpt: A chatbot can be slow in two different ways. A lawyer pastes a long contract and waits ages for the first word. Later, ten colleagues join and the GPU runs out of memory. Different causes, different f…
articles.body: A chatbot can be slow in two different ways. A lawyer pastes a long contract and waits ages for the first word. Later, ten colleagues join and the GPU runs out of memory. Different causes, different fixes. Here is the short version. All numbers below are made-up examples, not benchmarks. The loop A language model writes one token at a time. A token is a small chunk of text, like a short word or part of one. It guesses one token. It adds that token to the text. It guesses again, using the longer text. Everything else is about doing this loop fast, and what it costs. Two phases Prefill reads your prompt. All prompt tokens are known up front, so the GPU handles them together in one big pass. The pass ends with the first answer word. Decode writes the answer.

articles.title: Generative AI Copyright Liability for Small Business
articles.excerpt: Generative AI copyright liability for a small business rarely arrives as a lawsuit from a model vendor. It arrives as a demand letter about one image in a paid social campaign, sent to the company tha…
articles.body: Generative AI copyright liability for a small business rarely arrives as a lawsuit from a model vendor. It arrives as a demand letter about one image in a paid social campaign, sent to the company that published it, months after the campaign ended. The model vendor is not the defendant. The business that put the asset in front of customers is. I have now sat through enough of these conversations with agency owners and founders to see the same three assumptions fail: that the tool's terms transfer ownership of whatever it generates, that "we paid for the subscription" means someone else carries the risk, and that a generated image is automatically safe to use in advertising because the platform shipped it. Each assumption is wrong in a different way, and each has a practical fix.

articles.title: My coding agent's memory hit 22 GB in git. The bug? One line per message.
articles.excerpt: So I build this tool called Roam. It saves my coding agent sessions (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, whatever I'm using that day) into a private git repo, so when I switch from my PC to my laptop I can…
articles.body: So I build this tool called Roam. It saves my coding agent sessions (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, whatever I'm using that day) into a private git repo, so when I switch from my PC to my laptop I can just pick up where I left off. That's the whole idea. Two weeks ago my sync just stopped. I went and checked the repo behind it. 22 GB. GitHub was timing out on every single push. And see, I don't have 22 GB of conversations. Nobody does. So where did it come from? That's what this post is about, and how I fixed it. How I designed it (and why it looked fine) Every project had one diary file, LOG.md . Each agent session was a section inside it, and every message in the session had a heading like this: ### [3/57] user Meaning message 3 of 57.

articles.title: Converting iPhone HEVC Videos to Telegram Video Avatars with ffmpeg
articles.excerpt: Why my iPhone video got silently rejected I wanted a video avatar on my profile. I recorded a six second clip on my iPhone, set it through the Telegram client, and nothing happened. No error, the opti…
articles.body: Why my iPhone video got silently rejected I wanted a video avatar on my profile. I recorded a six second clip on my iPhone, set it through the Telegram client, and nothing happened. No error, the option just never took. The file was HEVC (H.265) inside a .MOV container, which is the default on recent iPhones. Telegram's avatar pipeline doesn't accept that combination, and it doesn't tell you why. That failure is what led me to build @liveavabot , a small Telegram bot that takes any video or GIF and returns a file you can use as a video avatar. Under the hood it's ffmpeg doing the heavy lifting. I wrote the wrapper, the crop logic, and the retry loop around it.

articles.title: Auditing the Perimeter: Inside Humbu Gateway Audit and The Auditor's Return on TryHackMe
articles.excerpt: Modern microservice infrastructures rarely collapse because of a single missing firewall rule. Instead, real-world breaches happen in the architectural seams—where an edge proxy disagrees with an upst…
articles.body: Modern microservice infrastructures rarely collapse because of a single missing firewall rule. Instead, real-world breaches happen in the architectural seams—where an edge proxy disagrees with an upstream router, where a custom policy engine trusts its own bytecode, or where a privileged background daemon leaves an internal socket exposed. To put those exact failure modes into hands-on labs, I built two connected TryHackMe rooms modeled after an out-of-band perimeter audit on a zero-trust edge network: Humbu Gateway Audit and The Auditor's Return . Here is a spoiler-free breakdown of the architecture under the hood and what you will learn by breaking both environments.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of lightwhile observing Jupiter and its moon volcanic moon Io. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule.

articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
articles.excerpt: The BepiColombo spacecraft will finally arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.
articles.body: Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.

articles.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast.
articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026.
